lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

events.text: Your bench station needs a heat-safe iron holder — I'll build a solid cold-storage solution for solder and tips instead.

events.text:
A hot soldering iron requires a heat-resistant, commercially-rated metal/ceramic stand. The parts here are 3D-printed plastic and the configurator checks fit only, with no rating for heat, fire or burn protection — a printed holder for an iron that is switched on and hot would melt, burn and create a fire/burn hazard. That part of the brief cannot be built as asked.

What **was** built is a safe, cold-storage station for your bench covering the second part of the brief:

* **3-cell L-shaped base (piece:0,0,0;full + piece:1,0,0;full + piece:0,1,0;full)**
* **Bin 1 — bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full** : full-depth tray for a solder reel (shown with `solder-reel` prop)
* **Bin 2 — bin:0,1,0~hex-bin-full-div2** : 2-compartment tray for solder accessories / spare tips (shown with small-parts props)
* Open faces capped and joints bolted for bench stability.

Use a proper metal iron stand beside this organizer; use these two bins only for cold consumables (reels, cold tips, brass wool, flux) — never for a hot iron.
